root_cause.text: The sigd_send() function in net/atm/signaling.c directly dereferences a vcc pointer from a userspace-provided message without validating that it corresponds to a registered VCC, allowing an unprivileged attacker to cause a kernel crash by supplying an arbitrary pointer via sendmsg().
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state: "The ATM send path (sendmsg -> vcc_sendmsg -> sigd_send) reads the vcc pointer from msg->vcc and uses it directly without any validation. This pointer comes from userspace via sendmsg() and can be arbitrarily forged." The patch introduces find_get_vcc() which "validates the pointer by searching through vcc_hash" and acquires a reference via sock_hold() if found, replacing the prior unchecked assignment `vcc = *(struct atm_vcc **)&msg->vcc;`.
